comment: Android's cameras for the Linux side's PipeWire camera nodes. capture-info (the platform bridge's socket, $RUNGIC_PLATFORM_SOCKET): whether the desktop is in front (visible), the camera permission and Android's cameras; shared/media/media-bridge.py starts one /usr/bin/rungic-camera-source ID WIDTH HEIGHT ROTATION FACING per listed camera while visible and permitted. camera (the capture socket /mnt/android-wayland/capture.sock, private to the app and the container): opens Android's camera ID; the reply line is its metadata with ok true and format android-yuv420, then frames until the connection closes, each big-endian: int32 magic 0x4d43414d, version 1, width, height, rotation, the three planes' row strides, pixel strides and lengths, int64 timestamp (ns), then the three planes (Y, U, V). shared/media/camera-source.cpp reads them into a PipeWire Video/Source node. Opening a camera turns on Android's camera indicator, so the provider check never sends it; acceptance camera.frames (front) and camera.back record frames from the node on the phone. Errors are {"error": string}, before any frame. Tested from both ends: tools/tests/test_contract_media.py (media-bridge.py against tools/contracts.py's stand-in; the frame reader camera-source.cpp needs PipeWire and is checked by camera.frames) and acceptance scenarios contract.camera (capture-info), camera.frames and camera.back.
